paper_metadata.title: Structure and properties of Ti-rich Ti-Zr-Nb-Mo medium-entropy alloys

evidence.quote: In this study, three nonequiatomic Ti-rich Ti–Zr–Nb–Mo medium-entropy alloys (Ti-MEAs), namely Ti50–Zr25–Nb15–Mo10, Ti58–Zr23–Nb12–Mo7, and Ti65–Zr20–Nb10–Mo5, were developed for biomedical applications.

In this study, the Ti-MEAs were as follows: Ti50–Zr25–Nb15–Mo10 (Ti50), Ti58–Zr23–Nb12–Mo7 (Ti58), and Ti65–Zr20–Nb10–Mo5 (Ti65) MEAs—respectively containing 34.06, 41.68, and 49.04 wt% Ti; 32.46, 31.5, and 28.76 wt% Zr; 19.83, 16.74, and 14.64 wt% Nb; and 13.65, 10.08, and 7.56 wt% Mo.

The Ti50, Ti58, and Ti65 MEAs were prepared using a commercial arc-melting vacuum pressure casting system (TAM-4S, Tachibana-Riko, Sendai, Japan) by using Ti (99.7 wt% pure), Zr (99.9 wt% pure), Nb (99.95 wt% pure), and Mo (99.95 wt% pure). All the Ti-MEAs ingots were melted more than six times for homogenizing the constituent elements.

The results revealed that all the as-cast Ti-MEAs exhibited a similar equiaxial grain structure and orientation. The grain sizes of Ti50, Ti58, and Ti65 were determined from the EBSD–IPF images. Ti65 exhibited a grain size of 19.7 ± 5.40 µm, which was greater than those of Ti50 (14.25 ± 4.0 µm) and Ti58 (14.46 ± 1.66 µm) because Ti65 exhibited the lowest δ.
